title: "True Positive"
description: "A positive prediction that correctly matches a positive ground-truth label."
term: "True Positive"
letter: "T"
category: "Model Evaluation"
difficulty: "Beginner"

## Simple explanation

A true positive is a case the model flags as positive that really is
positive. For example, a defect detector correctly identifies an item that
has a defect.

## Technical explanation

In binary classification, a true positive (TP) occurs when the predicted
class is positive and the reference label is positive. TP is one cell of
the confusion matrix and is used in metrics including precision, recall,
and F1.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Counting true positives shows how many target cases a classifier correctly
identifies. It must be interpreted with false positives and false
negatives, since the count depends on dataset size and class prevalence.

## How it works

Choose the positive class and decision rule, compare model predictions
with ground-truth labels, then count cases where both are positive. Report
the evaluation data and threshold so the count can be interpreted.

## Practical example

If a classifier marks 40 examples positive and 32 of them have positive
ground-truth labels, it has 32 true positives and 8 false positives. Its
precision is $32/40$.

## Common misconceptions

- A true positive is a count, not a rate; recall divides true positives by
  all actual positives.
- The label called “positive” is a task convention and may represent
  different outcomes in different applications.
